body: Project Sylpheed is Game Arts and SETA's Xbox 360 space-combat game, first released in Japan on 28 September 2006. The player flies the Delta Saber through a campaign set during an interstellar civil war, confronting fighter formations and much larger capital ships. It revisits the name and spirit of Silpheed while allowing movement in any direction instead of following the earlier series' scrolling route. A mission can fill the surrounding space with targets, making the first task one of orientation: find the important threat and understand where the player's ship belongs within the battle.

Weapons and augmentations change how the Delta Saber handles a particular assignment. Some objectives ask for enemy targets to be destroyed; others require friendly ships to remain alive. Secondary goals add further conditions, such as completing a task quickly or avoiding damage. The player has to read the mission as more than a collection of hostile objects. Protecting something can require abandoning a tempting target elsewhere, while a carefully selected weapon can make the necessary intervention more effective. Preparation and awareness work together to keep a large encounter under control.

Shinobu Gotou directed the sixteen-mission campaign, with animated scenes connecting the operations to its cast and political conflict. The score includes contributions from several Square Enix composers, among them Junya Nakano and Kumi Tanioka. Microsoft published the international editions in 2007. Critical responses varied between enthusiasm for its cinematic action and frustration with its complexity. The game offers a way to skip a mission after repeated failures, allowing the story to continue. Its distinctive ambition is to make a freely moving fighter feel like one small part of a much larger space battle.
